parallel.requirements: Recognized the required Node ESM translation, .mjs suffixes, manual process.argv parsing, no external dependencies, exact stdout/stderr behavior, local library split, and output placement under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while spawning /root/exe_probe for behavior probing; that child spawned a nested /root/exe_probe/exe_probe probe and then started its own implementation work before interruption.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented cli-spec, argv-parser, python-repr, errors, bidict, and test16.mjs, then patched bidict and error handling after identifying KeyAndValueDuplicationError behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent created the final module tree itself and listed the six files in /output; no child code artifact was integrated into the delivered tree.
parallel.verification: Verification covered the sample, help, missing/invalid args, --arg=value, duplicate options, duplicate keys, duplicate values, and the key-and-value duplication branch, but not the full official hidden suite.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 17 of 69 tests. The child's own implementation attempt was interrupted, but the parent had already produced a complete delivered artifact; the remaining likely gap is ordinary behavioral parity in hidden/error outputs.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual CLI, exact output, bidict clear/printing, and output-directory requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-actor workflow: probe executable behavior, design a parser and bidict clone, implement the module tree, run representative checks, and finalize.
serial.implementation: Implemented argSpec, cliSignal, cliParser, pythonString, bidictErrors, bidict, runTest16, and test16.mjs directly in one patch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The one actor assembled all modules and the entry point under /output and read back the final entry file before delivery.
serial.verification: Verification covered success, help, missing required args, invalid ints, --arg=value, ambiguous prefixes, option-like string values, negative integers, and duplicate-value cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 17 of 69 tests. The trace shows duplicate-error output checks remained less exact than Python's executable output, so this is an implementation fidelity gap rather than a coordination failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full prompt requirements and explicitly reported local .mjs ESM modules, manual argv parsing, no dependencies, and bidict behavior coverage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read the same prompt and reported local .mjs ESM modules, manual parsing, no dependencies, and bidict behavior coverage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both targeted the same task surface and both missed some official hidden acceptance behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent spawned /root/exe_probe, the first child spawned a nested probe, and the parent retained final implementation and delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had a single owner for probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added delegated behavior probing and an unfinished child implementation attempt, but ownership of the delivered artifact stayed with the parent; serial had no delegation overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The nested child returned a structured executable-behavior handoff, and the parent retrieved it through list_agents before the final KeyAndValueDuplicationError patch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all discovered behavior in one context and used it directly in its implementation plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a handoff boundary, but the important findings were available and aligned with the parent's later fix; no incompatible interface or lost requirement is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a six-file module set, then updated bidict/error handling to distinguish KeyAndValueDuplicationError from ValueDuplicationError.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote an eight-file module set separating arg spec, parser, signal, Python string rendering, bidict errors, bidict implementation, runner, and entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations used different internal module names and error-formatting approaches, but both modeled the same core parser and bidict operations and both still missed some official acceptance behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited too briefly once, then used list_agents to inspect the completed nested child result while the intermediate child remained running.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all observations and edits stayed in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra result-management overhead, including a timeout wait and an interrupted child, but the useful completed probe was visible to the parent before finalization.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the parent produced the delivered /output tree; the child traces show probing and no completed child code merged into the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and delivered its module tree directly in a single patch and later listed/read the produced files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision or shared-state contamination is evidenced. Parallel integration was parent-only despite concurrent child work, while serial had a simpler single-writer path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran representative Node checks after the final patch and then official evaluation failed 52/69.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran representative Node checks and then official evaluation also failed 52/69.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified a similar set of public and probed edge cases but neither ran an evaluator-aligned full suite before closure; both final official outcomes were identical.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed substantially more requests, tool calls, and tokens, including subagent work and a timed-out wait, but did not hit the host timeout and closed normally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with one actor, fewer requests, and no subagent overhead, but reached the same official score.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had higher overhead, yet no evidence shows deadline pressure displaced required final work; the shared 52/69 outcome points to implementation fidelity rather than budget exhaustion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both completed evaluations report solution_passed false with 52 of 69 tests passing. Parallel's main difference was delegated executable probing, including a nested child result that the parent retrieved through list_agents before a final duplicate-error patch. Serial kept the same probing and implementation in one actor. The similar final score is best explained by a shared ordinary implementation-fidelity gap in exact hidden/error-path behavior, not by a retained parallel coordination pattern.
parallel_contributors: Delegated probing produced useful behavioral findings, but the parent still implemented, patched, and verified the final artifact itself.
Parallel verified representative duplicate/error cases but did not run an evaluator-aligned full suite before closure.
serial_contributors: Single-actor probing and implementation avoided child lifecycle overhead.
Serial also relied on representative checks and did not clear the official hidden suite.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's final duplicate-error branch emitted Python-style traceback text for tested duplicate cases but the evidence does not show parity with the dynamic PyInstaller trailer present in executable crashes.
Serial's final duplicate-error checks emitted concise bidict error lines for some cases rather than the full executable traceback, yet official scoring still matched parallel at 52/69.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported common implementation-fidelity explanation, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parent created and patched the implementation itself; child implementation work was redundant rather than the only implementation owner.
There were not multiple completed component implementations requiring an unowned reconciliation step; the parent assembled the final tree.
The parent owned final file placement and produced /output/test16.mjs plus libraries before final response.
The parent carried the end-to-end path from probing through implementation, verification, file listing, and final delivery.
Executable probing was useful pre-implementation work, but the parent did not block all productive work behind a single mandatory gate with a concrete unfinished consequence.
Investigation and parent implementation overlapped, and the later implementation was completed and verified rather than left incomplete by a separate investigation phase.
The parent kept capacity on the critical implementation path and finished a deliverable; extra probing did not starve an indispensable correction path.
Two spawn calls and a timed-out 10 second wait increased overhead, but the run did not exhaust the task budget or lose finalization because of fan-out.
The first child had broad probing/implementation ambitions, but the parent did not depend on a lost child deliverable; no indispensable work remained unfinished because that child was oversized.
No directly visible omission from a child brief caused unusable work; the nested probe returned task-relevant CLI and bidict findings that the parent could use.
No separate child implementation was integrated with incompatible file names, exports, or interfaces; parent-owned files formed the delivered artifact.
The important nested-child findings were visible in the parent list_agents output; no known finding is shown disappearing through transfer.
The child result was lengthy but structured, and the parent acted on the key duplicate-error corner shortly after retrieving it.
The child findings described executable behavior, not a superseded workspace or implementation state consumed after becoming stale.
No incompatible child reports or contracts remained unadjudicated; parent and child observations agreed on the key parser and bidict behaviors.
The parent did run representative integrated checks before finalizing; the later official failure alone cannot establish a parent-visible unresolved global mismatch.
There was no replacement or retry agent repeating prior work without inherited checkpoints; child probing was concurrent, not a checkpoint-free retry.

The final duplicate-error patch was followed by Node verification runs, so no child result or implementation was merged only after verification.
No completed child implementation was retrievable and ignored; the only completed child result was executable findings, not code to join.
The completed verifier/probe finding from the nested child reached the parent through list_agents before closure.
The parent did not leave a required failed child scope unattended; it independently implemented and verified the deliverable despite child interruption.
The parent inspected available agent state and the completed nested result, then performed a related KeyAndValueDuplicationError correction.
The parent had one 10 second wait timeout, then immediately inspected agents; it was not near the decision deadline and no needed action was displaced.
No completed child file set or competing implementation path is shown conflicting with the parent's delivered files.
No two live agents are evidenced editing the same file and requiring reconciliation.
No non-entry module produced by another active agent was replaced or deleted by the parent.
The delivered entry point was created and patched by the parent; there is no evidence another agent owned or used an overwritten deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs from another agent.
Although agents shared /workspace, the trace shows no unstable provenance problem from concurrent unisolated writes.
No temporary file, cache, generated artifact, or auxiliary tool from one actor is shown being consumed by another as stable reference input.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The parent wait timeout, list_agents inspection, and first-child interruption are one lifecycle chain; it was reviewed under timing, failure propagation, monitoring, and load imbalance but rejected because no needed work was lost.
The child handoff and parent duplicate-error patch are one information-transfer chain; context labels were rejected because the information arrived and was used rather than lost or overloaded.

cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No label was retained solely for parallel use, higher token cost, child count, timeout wait, official failure, or ordinary implementation mismatch shared with the serial run.
